pages.title: Opening & The Creation
pages.content:
Adam (pbuh) is the first messenger of Allah and the father of all humans. Allah created him from soil and cared about him very much because he was the first human. We are the grandchildren of Adam (pbuh), so we can learn many lessons from this fantastic story. 

Allah created the sky and the earth. After that, He told the angels that He was going to create a human. He said, “The human is going to become the ruler on earth. The ruler is going to live on earth for many years.” Angels got surprised. They began waiting with curiosity. 

Then Allah’s angels collected soil from different parts of the earth, and Allah shaped Adam. Because of this, humans have different skin colors. 

Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) told us: “Allah created Adam (pbuh) from a handful of dust from different lands.” So the children of Adam (pbuh) are white, red, black, and yellow in color.

vocabulary.definition: A person chosen by Allah to teach people about Him.
Earth in which plants can grow.
The feeling of wanting to know or learn something.
The children of a person’s children.

exercises.title: Many Skin Colors
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 1.
exercises.question: Why are people’s skin colors not all the same?
options: Humans have lived on earth for many years.
Adam was made from soil from many parts of the earth.
The angels waited with curiosity for the new human.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1 says the angels “collected soil from different parts of the earth, and Allah shaped Adam. Because of this, humans have different skin colors.”

feedback.correct: Yes! The soil came from many places, so people have many skin colors. We are all children of Adam.
feedback.incorrect: Not this one. Read the third paragraph of Chapter 1 again and find the words “Because of this …”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Past Forms in the Story
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each verb from Chapter 1 with its past form.
languageFocusExercises.question: What is the past form of each verb?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: The story happened a long time ago, so the chapter uses past forms. Some verbs add -ed: create → created. Many common verbs change: say → said, begin → began, get → got.

feedback.correct: Good. You found the past forms that tell the creation story.
feedback.incorrect: Look at Chapter 1 again: “He said …”, “They began waiting …”, “Angels got surprised”, “Allah created …”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Past Event or Plan?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence from Chapter 1.
languageFocusExercises.question: Is it something that happened, or a plan for later?

formChoices.sentence: … Allah’s angels [choice] soil from different parts of the earth …
… He told the angels that He [choice] create a human.
… and Allah [choice] Adam.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Finished events in the story use the past: collected, shaped. “Was going to + verb” tells us about a plan for later, seen from the past: Allah told the angels about His plan before He created Adam. “He” needs “was”, not “were”.

feedback.correct: Well done. You chose the past for events and “was going to” for the plan.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second and third paragraphs of Chapter 1. Did it happen, or was it a plan for later?

languageFocusExercises.title: Linking Words
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the lines with words from the bank. One word is extra.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word fits each gap?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: … cared about him very much [blank] he was the first human. … the sky and the earth. [blank], he told the angels … soil from different parts of the earth … [blank], humans have different skin colors.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Because” gives a reason (why Allah cared about Adam). “After that” tells us what happened next. “Because of this” gives a result: Soil from different places → different skin colors.

feedback.correct: Correct. You used a reason word, an order word and a result word.
feedback.incorrect: Ask: Why? (reason) — What next? (order) — What happened as a result? Then check Chapter 1.

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: Retell the Creation Sequence
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Retell the start of the story in three or four short sentences.
languageFocusExercises.question: What happened, and what did Allah say would happen next?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong A2 response uses past verbs for finished events, a “going to” chunk for the announced future, and simple linkers such as “After that” or “Then”.

feedback.correct: Use accurate Chapter 1 language to organize the story clearly.

discussionPrompts.example: Allah created the sky and the earth.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what came next: “After that, He told the angels …”

pages.title: Knowledge and Respect
pages.content:
Allah told His angels, “After I have created Adam and given him life, show respect to him.” Adam could learn and understand. He was wiser than the angels because Allah gave Adam knowledge and taught him to think. He learned more than the angels knew. 

All the angels thought that Adam was amazing. They all admired him and respected him. But Iblis didn’t think so. Iblis thought Adam was an unimportant creature created from clay.

vocabulary.definition: The feeling that someone is important, shown by treating them well.
Things a person knows and understands.
Liked someone very much and thought they were great.
Soft earth that can be shaped.

hotspots.title: Knowledge
hotspots.description: Allah gave Adam (pbuh) knowledge and taught him to think.

hotspots.title: The Angels

exercises.title: Adam’s Knowledge
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 2.
exercises.question: Why did Adam know more than the angels?
options: Allah gave him knowledge and taught him to think.
He was created from clay and lived in Paradise before them.
The angels admired him, so they taught him the names of things.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2 says Adam “was wiser than the angels because Allah gave Adam knowledge and taught him to think.”

feedback.correct: Right! Allah gave Adam knowledge and taught him to think. That is why he learned more than the angels knew.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 2 again. Find the word “because” and read what comes after it.

languageFocusExercises.title: What Does “Could” Mean?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 2. True or false?
languageFocusExercises.question: “Adam could learn and understand.” This means Adam was able to learn and understand.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Could + verb” tells us what someone was able to do in the past. Adam was able to learn and understand because Allah gave him knowledge.

feedback.correct: Correct. “Could” shows Adam’s ability.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 2 again. “Could learn” = was able to learn.

languageFocusExercises.title: Wiser and More
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the lines with words from the bank. Two words are extra.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words go with “than” and after “taught him”?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: He was [blank] than the angels because Allah gave Adam knowledge and taught him [blank] think. He learned [blank] than the angels knew.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: We compare two things with “-er + than” (wiser than) or “more + than” (learned more than). “Wisest” and “most” compare one thing with all the others, so they do not go with “than”. After “taught + person”, we use “to + verb”: taught him to think.

feedback.correct: Well done. You used “wiser than”, “more than” and “taught him to”.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the first paragraph of Chapter 2. Which word goes with “than”?

languageFocusExercises.title: What Did Iblis Think?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put the parts in order to make the sentence from Chapter 2.
languageFocusExercises.question: What did Iblis think about Adam?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Thought + sentence” tells us someone’s opinion. The angels thought Adam was amazing. “But Iblis didn’t think so.” His opinion was different: He thought Adam was unimportant.

feedback.correct: Correct. “Iblis thought …” shows that this is only his opinion.
feedback.incorrect: Start with the person, then “thought”, then what he thought. Check the last line of Chapter 2.

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: Explain the Two Views
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Say three or four short sentences in your own words.
languageFocusExercises.question: What did the angels and Iblis think about Adam?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response combines ability, comparison, reason and contrast: what Adam could do, why he was wiser, what the angels thought, and what Iblis thought instead.

feedback.correct: Use accurate Chapter 2 language to connect ability, reason and contrasting opinions.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what Adam could do: “Adam could … and …”
discussionPrompts.example: Adam could learn and understand.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Compare: “He was wiser than … because …”
discussionPrompts.example: He was wiser than the angels because Allah gave him knowledge.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Give the angels’ view: “The angels thought that …”
discussionPrompts.example: The angels thought that Adam was amazing.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Give Iblis’s view: “But Iblis thought …”
discussionPrompts.example: But Iblis thought Adam was an unimportant creature.

I can say what someone could do and compare two people.
I can explain two different opinions.

pages.title: Iblis’s Arrogance
pages.content:
Then Allah asked Iblis, “Why didn’t you respect Adam?” Iblis said, “I am better than Adam. You created me from fire, and You created Adam from soil.” 

Iblis was arrogant. He thought he was more important and more valuable than Adam. He came from the fire and believed his origin was better. He thought little and was wrong about Adam. Iblis couldn’t see that Adam had perfect knowledge and it was for the good of every creature of Allah. This knowledge made Adam more valuable. 

For Allah, the clay or the fire did not make anybody valuable. But useful knowledge makes people great because with this knowledge, humans can do good and stop bad. 

But Iblis continued saying he was right and the Creator was wrong. Allah said to Iblis, “Go away! You are far from My love and care.” 

Adam was now in Paradise.

vocabulary.definition: Thinking you are better or more important than others.
Very useful or important.
A living being created by Allah.
The place or material something comes from.

hotspots.title: Fire and Soil
hotspots.description: Iblis compared fire with the soil from which Adam (pbuh) was created.

hotspots.title: “I Am Better”
hotspots.description: Iblis thought he was better than Adam (pbuh).

exercises.title: What Makes a Person Great?
exercises.instructions: Match each part with what Chapter 3 says about it.
exercises.question: What does Chapter 3 tell us about Iblis, Adam and real value?

matchingPairs.right: He said, “I am better than Adam.”
His knowledge was for the good of every creature.
It did not make anybody valuable.
With it, humans can do good and stop bad.

correctAnswer.Iblis: He said, “I am better than Adam.”
correctAnswer.Adam: His knowledge was for the good of every creature.
correctAnswer.Clay or fire: It did not make anybody valuable.
correctAnswer.Useful knowledge: With it, humans can do good and stop bad.

exercises.explanation: Iblis said he was better because he came from fire. But Chapter 3 says, “For Allah, the clay or the fire did not make anybody valuable. But useful knowledge makes people great because with this knowledge, humans can do good and stop bad.”

feedback.correct: Well done! Where we come from does not make us better. Useful knowledge and good actions do.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 3 again. The first paragraph has Iblis’s words, the second is about Adam’s knowledge, and the third is about clay, fire and useful knowledge.

languageFocusExercises.title: Iblis’s Idea or the Truth?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put each part from Chapter 3 in the right group.
languageFocusExercises.question: Is it only Iblis’s idea, or is it true?

items: He … believed his origin was better.
He thought he was more important …
Iblis continued saying he was right and the Creator was wrong.

dragDropGroups.group: What the chapter says is true
items: Adam had perfect knowledge and it was for the good of every creature of Allah.
For Allah, the clay or the fire did not make anybody valuable.

What Iblis thought: He … believed his origin was better.
He thought he was more important …
Iblis continued saying he was right and the Creator was wrong.
What the chapter says is true: Adam had perfect knowledge and it was for the good of every creature of Allah.
For Allah, the clay or the fire did not make anybody valuable.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Words like “thought”, “believed” and “saying” tell us that this is Iblis’s idea, not a fact. The chapter shows that his idea was wrong: “He thought little and was wrong about Adam.”

feedback.correct: Good. You saw that “thought”, “believed” and “saying” show Iblis’s own idea.
feedback.incorrect: Look for “thought”, “believed” or “saying”. They show what Iblis thought. Then read the second and third paragraphs of Chapter 3.

languageFocusExercises.title: Better, More Valuable, Couldn’t
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence from Chapter 3.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words compare, and which mean “was not able”?

formChoices.sentence: Iblis said, “I am [choice] than Adam.”
This knowledge made Adam [choice].
Iblis [choice] see that Adam had perfect knowledge …

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Good” has a special comparative: better. Long words like “valuable” use “more”: more valuable. “Couldn’t + verb” says what someone was not able to do in the past.

feedback.correct: Well done. You chose the correct comparisons and “couldn’t”.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first two paragraphs of Chapter 3 again and look for “than” and “couldn’t”.

languageFocusExercises.title: But and Because
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the lines with words from the bank. Two words are extra.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word shows a different idea, and which word gives a reason?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: … did not make anybody valuable. [blank] useful knowledge makes people great, [blank] with this knowledge, humans can do good and stop bad.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “But” shows a different idea: Clay or fire does not make anybody valuable, but useful knowledge makes people great. “Because” gives the reason: with this knowledge, humans can do good and stop bad.

feedback.correct: Correct. “But” shows the different idea, and “because” gives the reason.
feedback.incorrect: Read the third paragraph of Chapter 3. Which word shows a different idea? Which word answers “Why?”

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: Explain the Wrong Judgement
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Say three or four short sentences about Iblis’s mistake.
languageFocusExercises.question: What did Iblis believe, and why was he wrong?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong A2 response reports Iblis’s belief, uses one comparison, contrasts it with the chapter’s message, and gives a reason or result connected to useful knowledge.

feedback.correct: Use Chapter 3 language to report a belief, compare ideas, and explain a reason or result.

discussionPrompts.example: Iblis believed that his origin was better because he came from fire.

discussionPrompts.example: He thought he was more important than Adam.

discussionPrompts.example: But useful knowledge makes people great, not clay or fire.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Add a reason or result: “because …”, “can …” or “made …”
discussionPrompts.example: With useful knowledge, humans can do good and stop bad.

pages.title: Paradise and the Warning
pages.content:
Iblis got angry with Adam and hated him. He didn’t want Allah to be nice to Adam. Iblis thought Allah put him far from His love because of Adam. He waited for a chance. He wanted Adam to lose Allah’s love, just as he had. Allah told Adam to be careful about Iblis. 

Then, Adam started to feel lonely in Paradise. So, Allah gave him a wife. Her name was Eve (Hawwa). They started to live together in Paradise. It was more wonderful than we can imagine. All the gifts in Paradise were for them. But Allah had only one warning. He told Adam and Eve not to go near one tree.

vocabulary.definition: Sad because you are alone.
Very good and enjoyable.
A message about danger or something to avoid.
To make a picture of something in your mind.

hotspots.title: Eve (Hawwa)
hotspots.description: Allah gave Adam (pbuh) a wife named Eve.

hotspots.title: The One Tree
hotspots.description: Allah warned Adam (pbuh) and Eve not to go near one tree.

exercises.title: Adam and Eve
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 4.
exercises.question: Why did Allah give Adam a wife?
options: Allah wanted Adam to be careful about Iblis.
The angels asked Allah for another human.
Adam started to feel lonely in Paradise.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 4 says, “Adam started to feel lonely in Paradise. So, Allah gave him a wife. Her name was Eve (Hawwa).”

feedback.correct: Yes! Adam felt lonely, so Allah gave him Eve.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 4 again. How did Adam feel just before the word “So”?

languageFocusExercises.title: Who Did Iblis Want to Lose Allah’s Love?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 4. Choose the correct answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: “He wanted Adam to lose Allah’s love, just as he had.” Who did Iblis want to lose Allah’s love?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Want + person + to + verb” tells us what someone wants another person to do or to have happen. Iblis wanted Adam to lose Allah’s love. “Just as he had” means: Iblis had already lost it himself.

feedback.correct: Correct. The person after “wanted” is the one who should lose Allah’s love: Adam.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the word right after “wanted”. That person should “lose Allah’s love”. Check the first paragraph of Chapter 4.

languageFocusExercises.title: Want, Tell … To, Not To
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence from Chapter 4.
languageFocusExercises.question: What comes after “want/tell + person”?

formChoices.sentence: He didn’t want Allah [choice] nice to Adam.
Allah told Adam [choice] careful about Iblis.
He told Adam and Eve [choice] go near one tree.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: After “want + person” and “tell + person”, we use “to + verb”: wanted Adam to lose, told Adam to be careful. For a “do not” message, we put “not” before “to”: told them not to go.

feedback.correct: Well done. You used “to + verb” and “not to + verb” correctly.
feedback.incorrect: Remember: tell + person + to + verb, and tell + person + not to + verb. Check Chapter 4 again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Something New Begins
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put the parts in order to make the sentence from Chapter 4.
languageFocusExercises.question: What new feeling did Adam have?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Started to + verb” shows that something new begins: Adam started to feel lonely. Later, the chapter uses it again: “They started to live together in Paradise.”

feedback.correct: Correct. “Started to feel” shows a new feeling.
feedback.incorrect: Begin with “Then,” and the person. Then use “started to + verb”. Check the second paragraph of Chapter 4.

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: Give a Clear Warning
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say three or four short sentences about a warning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What does someone want, and what warning do you give?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong A2 response uses one “want + person + to” idea, one “started to” sentence, and a positive or negative instruction with “tell + person + (not) to”.

feedback.correct: Use the sentence starters to connect desire, change and warning clearly.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what someone wanted: “He wanted … to …”
discussionPrompts.example: My little brother wanted me to play football with him.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what changed: “Then … started to …”
discussionPrompts.example: Then it started to rain, and the street became wet.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Give advice: “I told … to …”
discussionPrompts.example: I told him to wear his raincoat.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Give a warning: “I told … not to …”
discussionPrompts.example: I told him not to run on the wet street.

pages.title: Satan’s Lie and Regret
pages.content:
When Adam and Eve were happy in Paradise, Iblis came near them and told them he was their friend. It was a big lie. He softly spoke to them: “If you eat from that one tree, you will never die.” 

After a while, Iblis finally made them believe his lie. They forgot Allah’s warning. Unfortunately, people are sometimes forgetful. 

Adam and Eve ate fruit from that banned tree. They made a mistake, but it wasn’t on purpose. They were very sad about their wrong action. They said sorry to Allah. They learned from their mistake and decided never to repeat it. They wanted Allah to excuse them. 

However, Iblis took an opposite direction. He never thought he was wrong because he was arrogant. He believed that he was superior to, smarter than and more important than the human. Iblis’ character makes it hard to do the right thing and see the difference between good and bad.

vocabulary.definition: Something you say that you know is not true.
Something you do that is wrong.
Often forgetting things.
Better or higher than someone or something.

hotspots.title: The Lie
hotspots.description: Iblis told Adam (pbuh) and Eve a lie about the tree.

hotspots.title: The Mistake
hotspots.description: Adam (pbuh) and Eve made a mistake and asked Allah to forgive them.

exercises.title: The Lie and the Mistake
exercises.instructions: Put the events from Chapter 5 in the right order.
exercises.question: What happened first, next and last?

sequencingItems.text: Iblis told Adam and Eve that he was their friend.
Adam and Eve forgot Allah’s warning.
Adam and Eve ate fruit from the banned tree.
Adam and Eve said sorry to Allah.

exercises.explanation: First Iblis came near them and said he was their friend. After a while, they believed his lie and forgot Allah’s warning. Then they ate from the banned tree. They were very sad and said sorry to Allah.

feedback.correct: Great! You followed the story from Iblis’s lie to Adam and Eve saying sorry.
feedback.incorrect: Follow Chapter 5 paragraph by paragraph: Iblis’s words, what Adam and Eve forgot, what they ate, and what they did when they were sad.

languageFocusExercises.title: If …, You Will …
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read Iblis’s words from Chapter 5. Is the statement true or false?
languageFocusExercises.question: Iblis said, “If you eat from that one tree, you will never die.” The “If …” part is what they must do first. The “will …” part is the result that Iblis promised.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “If + present verb …, … will + verb” joins a condition and a result. The “if” part says what must happen first (eat from the tree). The “will” part says what will happen next (never die). But Iblis’s promise was “a big lie”.

feedback.correct: Correct. “If you eat …” is the condition, and “you will never die” is the promised result.
feedback.incorrect: Read Iblis’s words in the first paragraph of Chapter 5. Which part comes first? Which part is the promise?

languageFocusExercises.title: Talking about a Mistake
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence from Chapter 5.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which forms tell us what Adam and Eve did and decided?

formChoices.sentence: They [choice] Allah’s warning.
They [choice] a mistake, but …
They learned from their mistake and decided never [choice] it.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Forget” has a special past form: forgot. In English we “make a mistake” (not “do a mistake”). After “decided (never)”, we use “to + verb”: decided never to repeat it.

feedback.correct: Well done. You used “forgot”, “made a mistake” and “decided never to”.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second and third paragraphs of Chapter 5 again. Remember: make a mistake, decide to + verb.

languageFocusExercises.title: What Do These Words Mean?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Find these words in Chapter 5. Match each one with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these words mean in the story?

matchingPairs.right: they did not plan to do it

correctAnswer.it wasn’t on purpose: they did not plan to do it

languageFocusExercises.explanation: These words help us follow the story. “After a while” shows time. “Unfortunately” shows a sad fact. “Banned” means not allowed. “It wasn’t on purpose” means they did not plan the mistake. “Took an opposite direction” shows that Iblis did the opposite of Adam and Eve: He never said he was wrong.

feedback.correct: Good. You understood the key words of Chapter 5.
feedback.incorrect: Find each word in Chapter 5 and read the sentence around it. What does it mean there?

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: Learn from a Mistake
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say four short sentences about a mistake you learned from.
languageFocusExercises.question: What was the mistake, and what did you learn?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong A2 response uses the chapter’s language to move from a past mistake to reflection and a future decision.

feedback.correct: Use the sentence starters to build a clear mistake-to-learning sequence.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say the mistake: “I made a mistake when …”
discussionPrompts.example: I made a mistake when I forgot my friend’s birthday.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say if you meant it: “It wasn’t on purpose.”
discussionPrompts.example: It wasn’t on purpose because I was very busy that week.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say what you learned: “I learned from …”
discussionPrompts.example: I learned from my mistake and wrote the date in my notebook.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Make a decision: “I decided not to … again.”

pages.title: Life on Earth
pages.content:
Allah excused Adam and Eve and put them on earth to live there. Allah taught them and gave them everything to rule on earth. They were the rulers of the planet Earth. They were going to direct and make everything better on the planet. They were using land to grow crops and keep animals. They were going to build houses, protect nature and help the weak. 

But Iblis also followed Adam and Eve on earth. He was still around. He wanted people not to remember Allah in their daily lives.

vocabulary.definition: Plants grown for food.
To lead or manage a place.
Everything around us that people did not make, such as land, water, plants and animals.
Not strong or needing help.

languageFocusExercises.title: What Does “Were Going To” Mean?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 6. Choose the best meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: “They were going to direct and make everything better on the planet.” What does “were going to” mean here?
options: They walked to a new place on the planet.
This was their work for the future on earth.
They did this before they came to earth.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Here “were going to + verb” does not mean moving to a place. It tells us about a plan or a job for the future, seen from the past. When Adam and Eve came to earth, this work was in front of them.

feedback.correct: Correct. “Were going to direct” tells us about their future work on earth.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the verb after “going to”: direct. It is a job for later, not a place. Check the first paragraph of Chapter 6.

languageFocusExercises.title: Their Plans on Earth
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put the parts in order to make the sentence from Chapter 6.
languageFocusExercises.question: What were Adam and Eve going to do on earth?

feedback.correct: Well done. You built a list of future jobs with “were going to”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Why? To … / Not To …
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence from Chapter 6.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words say why, and what Iblis did not want?

formChoices.sentence: Allah excused Adam and Eve and put them on earth [choice] live there.
Allah taught them and gave them everything [choice] rule on earth.
He wanted people [choice] remember Allah in their daily lives.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “To + verb” tells us why: on earth to live there, everything to rule on earth. We do not say “for live” or “for to live”. “Want + person + not to + verb” tells us what someone does not want another person to do.

pages.title: The First Messenger
pages.content:
Adam and Eve lived on earth for many years. They had good and hard days. Some days brought them peace, and some days were difficult. They also had lots of children. We are all their children. Then, Allah made Adam His first Messenger. He was the first Messenger of Islam. He started teaching people to be honest, do good, stop bad and always remember Allah. 

Adam (pbuh) and Eve taught their children to behave well for the love of Allah. They also taught them to thank Him for His help and the good things in life. They also warned their children against Iblis because Iblis was their enemy, not their friend. 

After the death of Adam (pbuh), Allah sent many other messengers. They taught the people right and wrong and the ways to stay away from Iblis. All the prophets took the same way. They wanted to make people remember Allah.

vocabulary.definition: Telling the truth and not cheating.
To act in a particular way.
A person who wants to harm or oppose someone.
A calm, quiet time with no fighting or worry.

exercises.title: A Warning for the Children
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 7.
exercises.question: Why did Adam and Eve warn their children against Iblis?
options: Iblis was their enemy, not their friend.
Iblis was the ruler of the earth.
The other messengers asked them to do it.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 7 says, “They also warned their children against Iblis because Iblis was their enemy, not their friend.” The other messengers came later, after Adam’s death.

They also warned their children [choice] Iblis …
… because Iblis was their enemy, [choice] their friend.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: We “teach + person + to + verb”: teaching people to be honest. We “warn + person + against + danger”: warned their children against Iblis. “X, not Y” says one thing is true and the other is not: Their enemy, not their friend.

feedback.correct: Well done. You chose “to”, “against” and “not”.
feedback.incorrect: Remember: teach someone to …, warn someone against …. Check the first two paragraphs of Chapter 7.

languageFocusExercises.title: Time and Life Words

feedback.correct: Good. You understood the time and life phrases of Chapter 7.

languageFocusExercises.title: From Adam to Later Messengers

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Then” shows the next step: After many years, Adam became the first Messenger, and he started teaching people. “After the death of Adam” moves to a later time, when other messengers came.

feedback.correct: Correct. You used the time words to put the story in order.
feedback.incorrect: Look for “Then” and “After the death of …”. Which event comes first? Check Chapter 7.

pages.title: Story of Habil and Qabil
pages.content:
Adam (pbuh) and Eve had two sons, Habil and Qabil. They were very different. Habil was kind, gentle and loved taking care of animals. Qabil was mostly jealous. When they grew up, Habil became a shepherd. He kept cows, sheep and other animals. Qabil was a farmer. He worked on the farm and grew crops. 

One day, they were in a serious disagreement. To solve the problem, they had to offer an offering to Allah. Habil brought his best and healthiest sheep as a gift for Allah, but Qabil brought just a handful of his crops. It wasn’t very valuable. Qabil didn’t care to please Allah and his father Adam (pbuh). Real goodness is giving the best and the most loved.

vocabulary.definition: A person who looks after sheep.
A person who grows crops or keeps animals on a farm.
Something given to Allah.
Unhappy because someone has something you want.

hotspots.title: Habil the Shepherd
hotspots.description: Habil cared for animals and brought his best sheep.

hotspots.title: Qabil the Farmer
hotspots.description: Qabil farmed the land and brought some of his crops.

exercises.title: Two Brothers, Two Offerings
exercises.instructions: Match each part with the right answer from Chapter 8.
exercises.question: What was each brother’s work, and what did he offer to Allah?

matchingPairs.right: just a handful of his crops

correctAnswer.Qabil’s offering: just a handful of his crops

exercises.explanation: Chapter 8 says Habil became a shepherd and Qabil was a farmer. “Habil brought his best and healthiest sheep as a gift for Allah, but Qabil brought just a handful of his crops.” The chapter ends: “Real goodness is giving the best and the most loved.”

feedback.correct: Well done! Habil gave his best. Real goodness is giving the best we have.
feedback.incorrect: The jobs are in the first paragraph of Chapter 8. The offerings are in the second paragraph.

languageFocusExercises.title: What Was He Like? What Was His Job?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put each part from Chapter 8 in the right group.
languageFocusExercises.question: Does it say what he was like, or his job?

items: When they grew up, Habil became a shepherd.

The person’s job: When they grew up, Habil became a shepherd.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Was + adjective” describes what a person is like: was kind, was jealous. “Was / became + a + job” tells us a person’s job: was a farmer, became a shepherd. “Became” shows a change: When they grew up, Habil started this job.

feedback.correct: Good. You saw the difference between “was kind” (what he was like) and “was a farmer” (his job).
feedback.incorrect: Look at the word after “was” or “became”. Is it a word like kind or jealous, or “a” + a job? Check the first paragraph of Chapter 8.

languageFocusExercises.title: Loved, Had To, Best
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence from Chapter 8.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word is correct in each sentence?

formChoices.sentence: … Habil was kind, gentle and loved [choice] care of animals.
To solve the problem, they [choice] offer an offering to Allah.
Habil brought his [choice] sheep as a gift for Allah …

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Love + verb-ing” tells us what someone enjoys: loved taking care of animals. “Had to + verb” says something was necessary in the past. “Good” has a special form: the best. “Healthy” becomes “the healthiest”.

feedback.correct: Well done. You chose “loved taking”, “had to” and “best and healthiest”.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 8 again. Remember: love + -ing, had to + verb, good → best.

languageFocusExercises.title: Two Different Gifts
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the line from Chapter 8 with one word.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word shows that the two brothers’ gifts were different?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: … as a gift for Allah, [blank] Qabil brought just a handful of his crops.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “But” joins two different ideas. Habil brought his best sheep, but Qabil brought just a handful of his crops. The chapter says: “Real goodness is giving the best and the most loved.”

feedback.correct: Correct. “But” shows the difference between the two gifts.
feedback.incorrect: Habil gave a lot, and Qabil gave a little. Which small word shows this difference? Check the second paragraph of Chapter 8.

discussionPrompts.example: My friend is kind, and she loves helping her grandmother.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what you must do: “I have to …”
discussionPrompts.example: I have to feed our cat every morning.

discussionPrompts.example: I try to give the best present I can because my friend is important to me.

pages.title: The First Crime
pages.content:
Allah was pleased with Habil’s offering because he gave from his heart. Qabil became very angry and said, “I will kill you.” When Habil heard this, he said, “I won’t fight back or harm you. You are my brother, and I fear Allah.” Qabil started fighting with his brother and hit him with a stone. Habil died there. 

Soon, Qabil was not angry anymore, and he felt so sad. But he also started to panic. He said, “I killed my brother. I did the worst thing in life. Now I don’t know what I should do with his dead body.” Then, Allah sent a crow. It landed on the ground near Qabil and started digging the ground. The crow showed Qabil the way to put his brother’s dead body in the hole. Qabil cried and said, “I am worse than this crow. I cannot hide my brother’s dead body.”

vocabulary.definition: A large black bird.
To suddenly feel so afraid that you cannot think clearly.
Making a hole by moving earth.
To hurt someone or cause damage.

hotspots.title: The Crow
hotspots.description: The crow showed Qabil how to bury his brother.

hotspots.title: Panic
hotspots.description: Qabil felt sad and afraid after he killed his brother.

exercises.title: Habil’s Answer
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 9.
exercises.question: Habil said, “I won’t fight back or harm you.” Why?
options: Qabil said sorry to him first.
Qabil was his brother, and he feared Allah.
Their father Adam told him not to fight.
exercises.explanation: Habil gave his reasons himself: “You are my brother, and I fear Allah.”

feedback.correct: Yes! Habil chose not to hurt his brother because he feared Allah.
feedback.incorrect: Read Habil’s words in the first paragraph of Chapter 9 again. Look at the sentence right after “I won’t fight back or harm you.”

languageFocusExercises.title: What Does “Won’t” Show?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read Habil’s words from Chapter 9. Choose the best meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: Habil said, “I won’t fight back or harm you.” What does “won’t” show here?
options: Habil says no: He will not do these things.
Habil was not able to fight because he was weak.
Habil talks about something he did before.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Won’t” = will not. “Won’t + verb” tells us about the future, and here it shows Habil’s clear choice: He refuses to fight back. He gives the reason: “You are my brother, and I fear Allah.”

feedback.correct: Correct. “Won’t” shows Habil’s choice not to fight back.
feedback.incorrect: “Won’t” is short for “will not”. It is about Habil’s choice now and in the future. Read his words in the first paragraph of Chapter 9.

languageFocusExercises.title: Feelings and Meanings
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Find these phrases in Chapter 9. Match each one with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these phrases mean in the story?

matchingPairs.right: he really wanted to give it
Even this bird is better than me.

correctAnswer.he gave from his heart: he really wanted to give it
correctAnswer.“I am worse than this crow.”: Even this bird is better than me.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The chapter shows feelings that change: Qabil was “not angry anymore” (his anger stopped), and he “started to panic”. “Worse than” is the opposite of “better than”: Qabil saw that even the crow knew what to do.

feedback.correct: Good. You understood how Chapter 9 describes feelings.
feedback.incorrect: Find each phrase in Chapter 9 and read the sentence around it. What does it mean there?

languageFocusExercises.title: Became, Should, Sent
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the lines with words from the bank. Two words are extra.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word fits each gap?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: Qabil [blank] very angry … “Now I don’t know what I [blank] do with his dead body.” Then, Allah [blank] a crow.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Become” and “send” have special past forms: became, sent. “Became + adjective” shows a change of feeling: Qabil’s feeling changed, and he became very angry. “I don’t know what I should do” shows that Qabil did not know the right action and needed help.

feedback.correct: Correct. You used “became”, “should” and “sent”.
feedback.incorrect: Remember: become → became, send → sent. Then find Qabil’s words about what to do in Chapter 9.

pages.title: The Story of Adam (pbuh)
pages.content:
He went far away. Adam (pbuh) became very sad. He lost both of his sons on the same day. The story tells us that good people should stay away from jealousy and not get angry quickly. 

Adam was a Messenger of Allah and the father of his other children. He had to continue his life. He got old over the years. His children and grandchildren took his message all over the world. This message still advises people to love and respect Allah. It tells them to be well-behaved and kind to others. 

Allah never leaves people alone. The stories of His messengers help us to live an honest life.

vocabulary.definition: A feeling of being unhappy and angry because someone has something you want.
Tells someone what they should do.
Polite and good in the way you act.
An important idea that is shared with others.

languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each verb from Chapter 10 with its past form.
languageFocusExercises.question: What is the past form of each verb?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: These verbs have special past forms: go → went, become → became, lose → lost, take → took (“His children and grandchildren took his message all over the world”).

feedback.correct: Good. You found the past forms in Chapter 10.

languageFocusExercises.title: Should, Had To, Still

formChoices.sentence: The story tells us that good people [choice] stay away from jealousy and not get angry quickly.

This message [choice] advises people to love and respect Allah.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Should + verb” gives advice (no “to” after should). “Had to + verb” says something was necessary in the past. “Still” shows that something continues until now: The message did not stop.

feedback.correct: Well done. You chose “should”, “had to” and “still”.

exercises.title: The Angels
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer.
exercises.question: Allah told the angels that He was going to create a human. How did the angels feel?
options: They were angry and afraid of the new human.
They were sad and did not want to see him.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1: “Angels got surprised. They began waiting with curiosity.”

feedback.correct: Yes! The angels were surprised, and they waited with curiosity to see the new creature.
feedback.incorrect: Not this one. Read the second paragraph of Chapter 1 again. What did the angels do after Allah spoke?

exercises.title: Everyone Admired Adam?
exercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Is it true or false?
exercises.question: All the angels and Iblis admired Adam.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: “All the angels thought that Adam was amazing.” But: “Iblis didn’t think so. Iblis thought Adam was an unimportant creature created from clay.”

feedback.correct: Right, it is false. The angels admired Adam, but Iblis did not. He thought Adam was unimportant.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 2 again. Did Iblis think the same as the angels?

exercises.title: Iblis Is Sent Away
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer.
exercises.question: Why did Allah send Iblis away?
options: Iblis ate fruit from the banned tree.
Iblis hurt Adam and Eve in Paradise.
Iblis kept saying that he was right.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 3: “But Iblis continued saying he was right and the Creator was wrong.” After that, Allah sent him away from His love and care.

feedback.correct: Yes. Iblis was arrogant. He did not say sorry. He kept saying he was right.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Read the end of Chapter 3 again. What did Iblis continue saying?

exercises.title: Iblis and Adam
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer.
exercises.question: Why did Iblis hate Adam?
options: Adam told the angels bad things about him.
Adam took the best place in Paradise from him.
He thought he lost Allah’s love because of Adam.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 4: “Iblis thought Allah put him far from His love because of Adam.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Iblis blamed Adam. He did not see that his own arrogance was the real problem.
feedback.incorrect: Not this one. Read the first paragraph of Chapter 4 again. What did Iblis think about Adam?

exercises.title: The Mistake
exercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Is it true or false?
exercises.question: Adam and Eve ate from the tree on purpose because they wanted to disobey Allah.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 5: “They forgot Allah’s warning.” And: “They made a mistake, but it wasn’t on purpose.”

feedback.correct: Right, it is false. Adam and Eve forgot the warning. Their mistake was not on purpose, and they were very sorry.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 5 again. Did Adam and Eve remember Allah’s warning? Was their mistake on purpose?

exercises.title: The First Messenger
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer.
exercises.question: What did Adam (pbuh) teach people as the first Messenger?
options: to build big houses and grow crops
to be honest, do good and remember Allah
to stay in one place and never travel
exercises.explanation: Chapter 7: “He started teaching people to be honest, do good, stop bad and always remember Allah.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Adam (pbuh) taught people to be honest, to do good, to stop bad and to always remember Allah.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Read the first paragraph of Chapter 7 again. What did Adam (pbuh) start teaching people?

exercises.title: Other Messengers
exercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Is it true or false?
exercises.question: After Adam (pbuh), Allah sent other messengers, and they taught the same way.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 7: “After the death of Adam (pbuh), Allah sent many other messengers.” And: “All the prophets took the same way. They wanted to make people remember Allah.”

feedback.correct: Right, it is true. All the prophets took the same way. They wanted people to remember Allah.
feedback.incorrect: Read the last paragraph of Chapter 7 again. What did all the prophets want?

exercises.title: A Sad Father
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer.
exercises.question: Why did Adam (pbuh) become very sad at the end of the story?
options: His children did not want to hear his message.
He lost both of his sons on the same day.
He had to leave his home and go far away.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 10: “Adam (pbuh) became very sad. He lost both of his sons on the same day.” Habil died, and Qabil went far away.

feedback.correct: Yes. Habil died, and Qabil went far away. Adam (pbuh) lost both sons on one day.
feedback.incorrect: Not this one. Read the first paragraph of Chapter 10 again. What happened to Adam’s two sons?

pages.title: Vocabulary Challenge
pages.content: Match six key words from the story with their meanings.

vocabularyPairs.meaning: The children of a person’s children.
vocabularyPairs.context: We are the grandchildren of Adam (pbuh), so we can learn many lessons from this fantastic story.

vocabularyPairs.meaning: The place or material something comes from.
vocabularyPairs.context: Iblis came from the fire and believed his origin was better.
It was more wonderful than we can imagine.

vocabularyPairs.meaning: To hurt someone or cause damage.
vocabularyPairs.context: I won’t fight back or harm you.

vocabularyPairs.meaning: A feeling of being unhappy and angry because someone has something you want.
vocabularyPairs.context: The story tells us that good people should stay away from jealousy and not get angry quickly.

pages.title: Language Review
pages.content: Review and use the grammar patterns and language functions from all ten chapters.

exercises.title: Look: Finished or Still to Come?
exercises.instructions: Put each sentence from the book in the right group.
exercises.question: Did it happen, or is it going to happen later?

items: He got old over the years.

dragDropGroups.group: It is still to come (will / won’t / going to)
items: They were going to build houses …
“I won’t fight back or harm you.”

It happened (past verb): He got old over the years.
It is still to come (will / won’t / goin: They were going to build houses …
“I won’t fight back or harm you.”

exercises.explanation: Past verbs (got, forgot) tell us that something happened and finished. “Will” and “won’t” (= will not) talk about later: A promise or a clear choice. “Were going to + verb” is a plan for later, seen from the past: when Adam and Eve came to earth, this work was in front of them.

feedback.correct: Well done. Past verbs for finished events; will, won’t and going to for later.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the verb. Is it a past form like got, or does it have will, won’t or going to before it?

exercises.title: Look: Able, Necessary or Good Advice?
exercises.instructions: Match each sentence from the book with its meaning.
exercises.question: What do could, couldn’t, had to and should mean?

matchingPairs.right: He was able to do it.

matchingPairs.left: Iblis couldn’t see that Adam had perfect knowledge …
To solve the problem, they had to offer an offering to Allah.
matchingPairs.right: It was necessary. There was no other way.

matchingPairs.left: … good people should stay away from jealousy …
matchingPairs.right: This is good advice for everyone.

He was able to do it.
correctAnswer.To solve the problem, they had to offer: It was necessary. There was no other way.
correctAnswer.… good people should stay away from jeal: This is good advice for everyone.

exercises.explanation: “Could + verb” = was able to. “Couldn’t + verb” = was not able to. “Had to + verb” = it was necessary in the past. “Should + verb” gives advice. After could, couldn’t and should, the verb has no “to”.

feedback.correct: Correct. Could and couldn’t for ability, had to for necessity, should for advice.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the small word before the verb: could, couldn’t, had to or should. Check Chapters 2, 3, 8 and 10.

exercises.title: Look: Better Than or the Best?
exercises.instructions: Read the three parts. Then choose the best answer.
exercises.question: Which part compares one thing with ALL the others, not with only one other thing?
options: He was wiser than the angels because Allah gave Adam knowledge …
“I am better than Adam. You created me from fire …”
Habil brought his best and healthiest sheep …
exercises.explanation: “-er + than” (wiser than) and “better than” compare two: Adam and the angels, Iblis and Adam. “The best” and “-est” (the healthiest) compare one thing with all the others: Habil had no sheep better than this one. Some words have special forms: good → better → the best.

feedback.correct: Correct. “Than” compares two; “best” and “-est” mean number one of all.
feedback.incorrect: Look for the word “than”. Which part has no “than” and uses “best” and “-est”?

exercises.title: Practise: So, But, Because
exercises.instructions: Complete the sentences with words from the bank. Two words are extra.
exercises.question: Which word fits each gap?
exercises.fillBlanksText: We are the grandchildren of Adam (pbuh), [blank] we can learn many lessons from this fantastic story. … They all admired him and respected him. [blank] Iblis didn’t think so. … They also warned their children against Iblis, [blank] Iblis was their enemy, not their friend.
exercises.explanation: “So” gives a result: We are Adam’s grandchildren, so we can learn from his story. “But” gives a different idea: The angels admired Adam, but Iblis did not. “Because” + a sentence gives a reason: Iblis was their enemy. “Because of” needs a noun after it (“because of Adam”), not a sentence.

feedback.correct: Well done. You linked a result, a different idea and a reason.
feedback.incorrect: For each gap, ask: Does the next part give a result, a different idea or a reason? Check Chapters 1, 2 and 7.

exercises.title: Practise: What Comes After the Verb?
exercises.instructions: Choose the correct form to complete each sentence from the book.
exercises.question: After “wanted Adam”, “started” and “advises people”, which form comes next?

formChoices.sentence: He wanted Adam [choice] Allah’s love, just as he had.
It landed on the ground near Qabil and started [choice] the ground.
This message still advises people [choice] and respect Allah.

exercises.explanation: After “want + person” and “advise + person”, use “to + verb”: wanted Adam to lose, advises people to love. After “start”, use verb-ing (started digging) or “to + verb” (“Adam started to feel lonely”). Never use the past form after “started”.

feedback.correct: Correct. Want and advise + person + to; start + -ing.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the verb before the gap: wanted Adam …, started …, advises people …. Check Chapters 4, 9 and 10.

exercises.title: Practise: Fix One Mistake
exercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
exercises.question: Can you fix the verbs and the comparing word?

errorItems.sentence: He losed both of his sons on the same day.
He believed that he was superior to, more smarter than and more important than the human.

exercises.explanation: “Begin” and “lose” change in the past: began, lost (not beginned, losed). Short words like “smart” add -er: smarter than. Do not use “more” and “-er” together. Long words use “more”: more important than.

feedback.correct: Well done. You fixed all three sentences.
feedback.incorrect: Compare with the book: Chapter 1 (the angels), Chapter 10 (Adam’s sons) and Chapter 5 (what Iblis believed).

exercises.title: Practise: Adam Starts Teaching
exercises.instructions: Put the parts in order to make the sentence from Chapter 7.
exercises.question: What did Adam start to do?
sentenceChunks: to be honest, do good, stop bad
exercises.explanation: “Started + verb-ing” shows that something new began: started teaching. “Teach + person + to + verb” tells us what people learn to do: teaching people to be honest. One “to” can go with a list of verbs: to be honest, do good, stop bad and always remember Allah.

feedback.correct: Well done. Started teaching … people to … .
feedback.incorrect: Start with “He started”. Then say who he was teaching, and what he taught them to do.

exercises.title: Use: Trees for Our School
exercises.instructions: Complete this new text from the word bank. Two words are extra.
exercises.question: Can you use the book’s words in a school story?
exercises.fillBlanksText: Last Friday, our class was going to plant trees in the school garden. But it rained, [blank] we [blank] stay inside. On Monday, our teacher told us [blank] bring old gloves. The work was [blank] than we thought, but everyone helped, and now our garden looks better.
exercises.explanation: “So” gives the result of the rain. “Had to + verb” says that it was necessary. “Told us to + verb” gives the teacher’s instruction. “Hard” is a short word, so we say “harder than”, not “more hard than”. The text also uses “was going to” for a plan that changed.

feedback.correct: Well done. You used the book’s language in a new place.
feedback.incorrect: Ask for each gap: A result or a reason? Was it necessary? What comes after “told us”? How do we compare with a short word?

exercises.title: Use: A Plan That Changed
exercises.instructions: Write 4–5 sentences about a changed plan. Tell a partner first.
exercises.question: What was your plan, and what happened?
exercises.explanation: Example: “Last Saturday, I was going to play football with my friends. But my little brother was ill, so I had to stay at home. I couldn’t go out, but I read a story to him. My mother told me not to worry. The day was better than I thought.”

feedback.correct: Check your sentences: was going to, past verbs, so / but / because, had to / couldn’t, told me (not) to, better than / -er than.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Give the plan: “Last …, I was going to …”
discussionPrompts.example: Last Saturday, I was going to play football in the park.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what happened: “But …, so I had to …” or “I couldn’t …”
discussionPrompts.example: But it started to rain, so I had to stay at home.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Give someone’s advice: “My mother told me to … / not to …”
discussionPrompts.example: My mother told me not to go out in the rain.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Compare: “The day was better / harder than I thought.”
discussionPrompts.example: The day was better than I thought because I read a good book.

pages.title: Master Glossary
pages.content: Review all key vocabulary from the story in one place.

vocabulary.definition: A person chosen by Allah to teach people about Him.
vocabulary.storyExample: Adam (pbuh) is the first messenger of Allah and the father of all humans.

vocabulary.definition: Earth in which plants can grow.
vocabulary.storyExample: Allah created him from soil and cared about him very much because he was the first human.

vocabulary.definition: The feeling of wanting to know or learn something.
vocabulary.storyExample: They began waiting with curiosity.

vocabulary.definition: The children of a person’s children.
vocabulary.storyExample: We are the grandchildren of Adam (pbuh), so we can learn many lessons from this fantastic story.

vocabulary.definition: The feeling that someone is important, shown by treating them well.
vocabulary.storyExample: Allah told His angels, “After I have created Adam and given him life, show respect to him.”

vocabulary.definition: Things a person knows and understands.
vocabulary.storyExample: He was wiser than the angels because Allah gave Adam knowledge and taught him to think.

vocabulary.definition: Liked someone very much and thought they were great.
vocabulary.storyExample: They all admired him and respected him.

vocabulary.definition: Soft earth that can be shaped.
vocabulary.storyExample: Iblis thought Adam was an unimportant creature created from clay.

vocabulary.definition: Thinking you are better or more important than others.
vocabulary.storyExample: Iblis was arrogant.

vocabulary.definition: Very useful or important.
vocabulary.storyExample: He thought he was more important and more valuable than Adam.

vocabulary.definition: A living being created by Allah.
vocabulary.storyExample: Iblis couldn’t see that Adam had perfect knowledge and it was for the good of every creature of Allah.

vocabulary.definition: The place or material something comes from.
vocabulary.storyExample: He came from the fire and believed his origin was better.

vocabulary.definition: Sad because you are alone.
vocabulary.storyExample: Then, Adam started to feel lonely in Paradise.

vocabulary.definition: Very good and enjoyable.
vocabulary.storyExample: It was more wonderful than we can imagine.

vocabulary.definition: A message about danger or something to avoid.
vocabulary.storyExample: But Allah had only one warning.

vocabulary.definition: To make a picture of something in your mind.
vocabulary.storyExample: It was more wonderful than we can imagine.

vocabulary.definition: Something you say that you know is not true.
vocabulary.storyExample: It was a big lie.

vocabulary.definition: Something you do that is wrong.
vocabulary.storyExample: They made a mistake, but it wasn’t on purpose.

vocabulary.definition: Often forgetting things.
vocabulary.storyExample: Unfortunately, people are sometimes forgetful.

vocabulary.definition: Better or higher than someone or something.
vocabulary.storyExample: He believed that he was superior to, smarter than and more important than the human.

vocabulary.definition: Plants grown for food.
vocabulary.storyExample: They were using land to grow crops and keep animals.

vocabulary.definition: To lead or manage a place.
vocabulary.storyExample: Allah taught them and gave them everything to rule on earth.

vocabulary.definition: Everything around us that people did not make, such as land, water, plants and animals.
vocabulary.storyExample: They were going to build houses, protect nature and help the weak.

vocabulary.definition: Not strong or needing help.
vocabulary.storyExample: They were going to build houses, protect nature and help the weak.

vocabulary.definition: Telling the truth and not cheating.
vocabulary.storyExample: He started teaching people to be honest, do good, stop bad and always remember Allah.

vocabulary.definition: To act in a particular way.
vocabulary.storyExample: Adam (pbuh) and Eve taught their children to behave well for the love of Allah.

vocabulary.definition: A person who wants to harm or oppose someone.
vocabulary.storyExample: Iblis was their enemy, not their friend.

vocabulary.definition: A calm, quiet time with no fighting or worry.
vocabulary.storyExample: Some days brought them peace, and some days were difficult.

vocabulary.definition: A person who looks after sheep.
vocabulary.storyExample: When they grew up, Habil became a shepherd.

vocabulary.definition: A person who grows crops or keeps animals on a farm.
vocabulary.storyExample: Qabil was a farmer.

vocabulary.definition: Something given to Allah.
vocabulary.storyExample: To solve the problem, they had to offer an offering to Allah.

vocabulary.definition: Unhappy because someone has something you want.
vocabulary.storyExample: Qabil was mostly jealous.

vocabulary.definition: A large black bird.
vocabulary.storyExample: Then, Allah sent a crow.

vocabulary.definition: To suddenly feel so afraid that you cannot think clearly.
vocabulary.storyExample: But he also started to panic.

vocabulary.definition: Making a hole by moving earth.
vocabulary.storyExample: It landed on the ground near Qabil and started digging the ground.

vocabulary.definition: To hurt someone or cause damage.
vocabulary.storyExample: I won’t fight back or harm you.

vocabulary.definition: A feeling of being unhappy and angry because someone has something you want.
vocabulary.storyExample: The story tells us that good people should stay away from jealousy and not get angry quickly.

vocabulary.definition: Tells someone what they should do.
vocabulary.storyExample: This message still advises people to love and respect Allah.

vocabulary.definition: Polite and good in the way you act.
vocabulary.storyExample: It tells them to be well-behaved and kind to others.

vocabulary.definition: An important idea that is shared with others.
vocabulary.storyExample: His children and grandchildren took his message all over the world.

pages.title: Final Challenge
pages.content: Show what you learned across the whole story with ten different scored activities.

exercises.title: A Job on Earth
exercises.instructions: Complete Allah’s words from Chapter 1 with one word: ruler, angel or farmer.
exercises.question: What did Allah say about the new human?
exercises.fillBlanksText: The human is going to become the [blank] on earth.
exercises.explanation: In Chapter 1 Allah says: “The human is going to become the ruler on earth.”

feedback.correct: Yes. From the start, Allah gives the human an important job on earth.
feedback.incorrect: Read what Allah tells the angels in Chapter 1. What will the human become on earth?

exercises.title: How Iblis Saw Adam
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer from Chapter 2.
exercises.question: Why did Iblis think Adam was not important?
options: Adam could not learn new things.
The angels did not like Adam.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2 says: “Iblis thought Adam was an unimportant creature created from clay.” But the same chapter says Adam “could learn and understand”, and the angels “admired him and respected him”.

feedback.correct: Yes. Iblis looked only at the clay. He did not see Adam’s knowledge.
feedback.incorrect: Read the last sentence of Chapter 2. What did Iblis look at when he thought about Adam?

exercises.title: One Warning
exercises.instructions: Is this sentence true or false?
exercises.question: In Paradise, Adam and Eve could eat from every tree.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 4 says: “All the gifts in Paradise were for them. But Allah had only one warning. He told Adam and Eve not to go near one tree.”

feedback.correct: Right. Almost everything was for them, but Allah told them not to go near one tree.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of Chapter 4. What was Allah’s only warning?

exercises.title: Adam’s Life in Order
exercises.instructions: Put these events in the correct order.
exercises.question: What happened first, next and later in Adam’s life?

sequencingItems.text: Adam and Eve eat from the banned tree.
Allah makes Adam His first Messenger.
Allah gives Adam a wife, Eve.
Adam and Eve start to live on earth.
The angels respect Adam, but Iblis does not.

exercises.explanation: Allah shapes Adam (Chapter 1), the angels respect him but Iblis does not (Chapter 2), Allah gives him Eve (Chapter 4), they eat from the tree (Chapter 5) and live on earth (Chapter 6). After many years, “Allah made Adam His first Messenger” (Chapter 7).

feedback.correct: Yes. Adam became a Messenger on earth, after many years there.
feedback.incorrect: Start with Chapter 1. Then remember: Adam became the first Messenger after he and Eve “lived on earth for many years”.

exercises.title: Rulers of the Earth
exercises.instructions: Match each thing with what Adam and Eve did with it.
exercises.question: What did Adam and Eve do on earth?

matchingPairs.right: used it to grow crops and keep animals

correctAnswer.land: used it to grow crops and keep animals

exercises.explanation: Chapter 6 says: “They were using land to grow crops and keep animals. They were going to build houses, protect nature and help the weak.”

feedback.correct: Yes. As rulers, Adam and Eve took care of the earth and the people on it.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 6 again. Find each word: land, houses, nature, the weak.

exercises.title: After the Mistake
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer from Chapter 5.
exercises.question: After the mistake, how were Adam and Eve different from Iblis?
options: They blamed Iblis, and Iblis said sorry to Allah.
They stayed quiet, and Iblis ran away from them.
They said sorry, but Iblis never thought he was wrong.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 5 says Adam and Eve “said sorry to Allah” and “learned from their mistake”. But Iblis “never thought he was wrong because he was arrogant.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Adam and Eve learned from their mistake. Iblis was arrogant and did not change.
feedback.incorrect: Compare the third paragraph of Chapter 5 (Adam and Eve) with the last paragraph (Iblis).

exercises.title: Real Goodness
exercises.instructions: Complete the sentence from Chapter 8 with one word: loved, expensive or beautiful.
exercises.question: What is real goodness, as Chapter 8 says?
exercises.fillBlanksText: Real goodness is giving the best and the most [blank].
exercises.explanation: Chapter 8 ends: “Real goodness is giving the best and the most loved.” Habil gave “his best and healthiest sheep”; Qabil gave “just a handful of his crops”.

feedback.correct: Yes. Real goodness means giving what we love most, like Habil’s best sheep.
feedback.incorrect: Read the last sentence of Chapter 8. What kind of thing is best to give?

exercises.title: The Crow
exercises.instructions: Is this sentence true or false?
exercises.question: The crow showed Qabil how to put his brother’s body in the ground.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 9 says Qabil did not know what to do. Then “The crow showed Qabil the way to put his brother’s dead body in the hole.”

feedback.correct: True. Allah sent a crow, and it dug the ground to show Qabil what to do.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of Chapter 9. What did the crow do near Qabil?

exercises.title: Words for Each Person
exercises.instructions: Match each person with the words the story uses for him.
exercises.question: Which words from the story describe each person?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: Adam “was wiser than the angels”. Chapter 3: “Iblis was arrogant.” Chapter 8: “Habil was kind, gentle and loved taking care of animals. Qabil was mostly jealous.”

feedback.correct: Yes. These words help us understand why each person acted the way he did.
feedback.incorrect: Look at Chapter 2 for Adam, Chapter 3 for Iblis and the start of Chapter 8 for the two brothers.

exercises.title: The Lesson for Us
exercises.instructions: Choose the lesson from Chapter 10.
exercises.question: What does the story of the two brothers teach good people?
options: Stay away from jealousy and do not get angry quickly.
Give your best gifts only to your own family.
Go far away from people after a mistake.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 10 says: “The story tells us that good people should stay away from jealousy and not get angry quickly.” Qabil was jealous and angry, and this led to the first crime.

feedback.correct: Yes. Jealousy and anger led Qabil to the worst thing in life.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 10. Find the sentence that begins “The story tells us”.
